answer: Every agent locks a marble, a small stake, in a public jar. A prism model splits each agent's activity into spectral bands: timing, vocabulary, tool-call order. Agents whose bands overlap are bundled into one plume, and every pair inside a plume owes a cross-audit fee paid from their marbles before either can earn. A lone agent owes nothing extra, but n fakes from one operator owe n(n-1)/2 fees, so the bill grows quadratically while honest diversity stays cheap.
